rows.n: calibration
rows.b: Whether the model's confidence matches its actual accuracy — a well-calibrated model knows when it is guessing.

rows.n: canary release
rows.b: Sending a new model to a small slice of users first to catch problems early.

rows.n: casing
rows.b: Whether the tokenizer distinguishes Apple from apple — a choice that changes the vocabulary.

rows.n: causal mask
rows.b: A rule during training that hides future tokens, so the model can only learn from the past — the way real generation works.

rows.n: CDN
rows.b: A content delivery network that serves static files, like model weights, from servers near each user.

rows.n: chain-of-thought prompting
rows.b: Asking the model to reason step by step out loud, which improves hard problems.

rows.n: character-level tokenization
rows.b: Tokenizing text one character at a time — simple, tiny vocabulary, and the approach Signature Llama v1 uses.

rows.n: checkpoint
rows.b: A saved snapshot of the model's parameters during training, so work is never lost and the best version can be kept.

rows.n: Chinchilla scaling
rows.b: The finding that models should be trained on far more tokens than was fashionable — about twenty tokens per parameter.

rows.n: chunk
rows.b: A fixed-size slice of text cut from documents to feed the model during training.

rows.n: classification token
rows.b: A special token whose final state is used as the summary of a whole input for classification.

rows.n: cold start
rows.b: The slow first request while a model loads into memory.

rows.n: commercial use
rows.b: Using a model to make money, which some licenses allow freely and others restrict.

rows.n: completion
rows.b: The text the model generates in response to a prompt.

rows.n: compression ratio
rows.b: How compactly a tokenizer encodes text, measured in characters per token.

rows.n: compute-optimal
rows.b: The sweet spot of model size versus training data for a fixed compute budget.

rows.n: containerization
rows.b: Packaging a model and its environment into a portable container that runs the same anywhere.

rows.n: contamination check
rows.b: Verifying the test questions were not hiding in the training data.

rows.n: context length
rows.b: How many tokens of conversation the model can actually keep in mind at generation time.

rows.n: context stuffing
rows.b: Packing background documents into the prompt so the model answers from provided material.

rows.n: context window
rows.b: The maximum number of tokens a model can consider at once, covering both the prompt and what it has generated.

rows.n: continual pretraining
rows.b: More pretraining on new data after the first round, e.g. to teach a model a specialty like medicine or law.

rows.n: continuous batching
rows.b: A server trick that slots new requests into the batch the moment old ones finish, keeping the GPU always busy.

rows.n: corpus
rows.b: A large collection of text assembled for training or study — the model's reading material.

rows.n: cosine schedule
rows.b: A learning-rate plan that follows a cosine curve: warm up, cruise, then glide smoothly down to near zero.

rows.n: cost per token
rows.b: The unit price of generation on hosted APIs, usually quoted per million tokens.

rows.n: CPU inference
rows.b: Running the model on the regular processor — slower than GPU but available everywhere.

rows.n: cross-attention
rows.b: Attention where the queries come from one sequence and the keys and values from another, linking e.g. a question to a document.

rows.n: cross-entropy loss
rows.b: The standard loss for language models: it punishes the model according to how unlikely it thought the true next token was.

rows.n: curriculum learning
rows.b: Feeding training data in order from easy to hard, the way a student learns.
